While STAGGERED the state is likewise unchanged. At the tick `emitter.place` reads `loco_state == DEAD`, it forces `switch_on` false (the Controller's `DEAD` row: "beam off (Emitter State on actor death)") as an `emitter.place`-internal `force_off`, a read of `controller.state` with no command. 212	**EM-10 — Beam charge is Suit's.** Suit & Equipment owns charge, drain, `CHARGE_EMPTY` and the HUD "beam and tool charge" reading (art bible HUD set). `toggle_beam.validate` reads Suit's charge view and rejects a turn-ON at zero charge with `CHARGE_EMPTY`; a turn-OFF is never rejected for charge (the strobe floor `TOO_SOON` of EM-7 applies to both directions). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Suit's divisor-6 `suit.vitals` reads `emitter.state.lit` on the seat's beam to drain charge and calls `force_off(beam_id)` (E5) at zero; because `suit.vitals` runs earlier in the tick than `emitter.place`, a `force_off` takes effect in the same tick's `emitter.place`, and the owner's six-tick re-check (EM-25) then finds a channelled target unlit and aborts, so at most five ticks of channel run on a dark target. The beam is a *suit load, not a ship LOAD*: Emitter State never calls `set_load_request` for it and the Graph is not involved. (Suit & Equipment, designed: SE-8; Suit keeps the hook name `suit.vitals` and its `after: graph.propagate.atmo`.)

214	**EM-11 — Fixtures are switchable Graph LOADs; the lamp formula gates on the switch.** A FIXTURE carries `node_ref` (a Graph `13 LOAD` node of the LOAD subtype `LAMP` — the Item DB assigns the subtype id, currently `2 LAMP`; the Graph names only `HEATER`; provisional), `base_pm` (from the def's `emits`) and `switch_on`. Its brightness is `lamp_output_pm` (Formulas D.1): `output_pm = switch_on and armed and live ? ⌊base_pm * served_pm / 1000⌋ : 0`. The lit branch is the registry formula `power_allocation`'s output "lamp brightness = base * served_pm / 1000", reused verbatim. **`served_pm` is the tier's satisfaction `sat_k`, independent of the node's own request** (Graph D.6), so a switched-off lamp can still read `served_pm` 1000: the Emitter's own `switch_on` is the gate, not the Graph, or an off lamp would shine. Power draw is a Graph LOAD: inside the `set_switch` apply the Emitter calls M14 `set_load_request(node_ref, req_w)` with `req_w` the def's rated draw (Graph MVP: 20 W) when on and 0 when off (Class B: it clamps to `0..req_max`, queues to the next Graph phase 0, and is a no-op on an unknown, tombstoned, dormant or SALVAGED node). A lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served (Graph P1); under re-energise inrush the bank draws `req_w * INRUSH_PM / 1000` for `INRUSH_STEPS` runs, which can dim the tier-3 bank for half a second — the Graph's business, visible as an honest dip, changing no Emitter rule. The Emitter never recomputes watts and never calls M14 for node lanterns or the beam. A FIXTURE with `node_ref` 0 is *self-powered*: permitted only for the two declared subkinds, EMERGENCY (the cryo-bay emergency lamp, exactly one in the world, declared by Derelict Authoring DA-23 as `fixture_subkind_emergency`) and DOCK_STATUS (below); it has no M14 call, no ARMING and a fixed `base_pm`, and any other `node_ref` 0 fixture is refused by the authoring lint and at boot (`SELF_POWERED_LAMP_COUNT`: exactly one EMERGENCY, exactly one DOCK_STATUS per dock room, none elsewhere). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; second subkind added 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2)* **The DOCK_STATUS fixture (user ruling X2, 2026-10-27)** keeps the pod console's lit gate satisfied at every dock without a further `act_gate` exception *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* (Interaction's IA-6 refusal of a `pod_hop` exemption stands): it is an *ordinary lit fixture* (`gates_actions` true, SOFT curve, counted in `lux_pm`, `act_lux_pm` and `section_emission`, so the web can read it like any lamp, P3 and "light is never free"), authored by Derelict Authoring on the dock room's docked-podcraft prop, in the **dock room's section** and not on the pod body (the pod section is dormant always, Web Map WM-5, and the lamp must not depend on it). It is created and discarded with its section (E1, E2), has no `node_ref` and therefore no liveness test (EM-13 concerns Graph nodes) and cannot be failed, starved or drained by any ship state, which is the point: the stranded player always finds the console lit. Its `switch_on` is driven only by the mutator **E10 `set_dock_status(section_id, on)`**, which Web Map & Transit calls in the apply that writes `pod_at` (on for the dock room the pod parks at, off for the one it leaves; the berth and unberth verbs are the derelict weld verbs and have nothing to do with it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the first draft named the berth and unberth applies, and read `pod_at` at E1)*, so the glow emits only while the pod is there. **E1 creates every DOCK_STATUS glow switched off and reads nothing of Web Map's state**: E1 runs at `init_world` step 2, before Web Map writes `pod_at` at step 7, so the home dock's glow is switched on by Web Map's step-7 call to E10 (`pod_at` HOME) in the same `init_world` apply, and the derelict docks' glows stay off until the pod parks there. `set_switch` of either origin is refused `NOT_SWITCHABLE` for this subkind and Interaction registers no switch interactable for it; it takes no M14 call and no ARMING, and E10 has no commit-spacing guard and writes no `last_toggle_tick` (E10's row in EM-5 gives the reason: the pod's own timing spaces the transitions, and an atomic apply could not observe a refusal) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **Values** (placeholders, owner game-designer and art-director, confirmed by the Lighting spike; derivation in D.1b): `DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM` 500, `DOCK_STATUS_REACH_PX` 48, shape row 7 (`FIXTURE`, SOFT) at that reach, and the placement constraint `DOCK_STATUS_CONSOLE_MAX_PX` 24 (the console subject's anchor lies within 24 px of the glow origin, clear of every occluder). Its luminance and hue sit outside the visible-unknown lamp's band (the art-director's, not this GDD's; a Lighting `hue_class` token owed). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

216	**EM-12 — One latency story for switching.** A `set_switch` applies at P2 of tick `T_a`; its M14 call is queued to the next Graph phase 0; the lamp is **ARMING with `output_pm` 0** until `arm_tick`, the first `graph.propagate.power` run that consumed the request, and is lit on the first `emitter.place` at or after it (Formulas D.2 `switch_latency`: `arm_tick = T_a + ((GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - (T_a mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)) mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`). Under the stated assumptions the lamp is lit between 0 and `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks after the apply — at most 83 ms — and no single number from this paragraph is a design fact: D.2 derives the range with a worked example at both alignments (switch on a Graph tick; switch on the tick after one). **Assumption A1 (derived, not assumed; confirmed by the Graph 2026-10-27 in its Interactions row for this system):** kernel CR-2 ("P3 sees all of P2") and Graph LS-8 phase 0 ("apply queued unconditional inputs: `set_load_request` changes") together mean that an M14 call made in P2 of a Graph tick is consumed by that same tick's phase 0, so the range is 0..`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks; the negative case, a Graph that applied only strictly later requests, would give 1..`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` and is kept in D.2 as the labelled alternative. The direct `after: graph.propagate.failure` entry (EM-1) guarantees that the hook reads that run's output on the same tick. Switching **off** is immediate (`output_pm` 0 from the apply tick; M14 `(node_ref, 0)`); an OFF applied while the lamp is still ARMING cancels the pending ON and is not a realised transition (it writes no `last_toggle_tick`, EM-7, D.2b). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D32)* The same "light changes only on committed state" rule PC-5 states for the beam holds for fixtures; the asymmetry (ON waits for the Graph pulse, OFF does not) is deliberate and physical: the ship has to serve the lamp, and the lamp cannot go on ahead of the ship. Fixtures never pre-play light; the wall-switch click and animation pre-play. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

218	**EM-13 — Liveness: a lamp is dark when its node is dead.** A lamp or lantern is *live* iff its `node_ref` exists and `node(id).state` is neither `3 DESTROYED`, `2 FAILED`, `4 SALVAGED` nor `5 ABSENT` (Graph LS-10) and the node is not dormant or tombstoned (read each tick from the Graph read view). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: 'live' is the output rule only. Command validation uses 'structurally present' (EM-7), which excludes SALVAGED, ABSENT, dormant and tombstoned nodes but not FAILED or DESTROYED ones, so a failed lamp can still be switched.)* A not-live lamp has `output_pm` 0 while its `switch_on` stays as committed — when the node is repaired the lamp lights again without a new command. `served_pm` and node `state` are read live each tick; both change only on Graph ticks, and because `emitter.place` is `after: graph.propagate.failure` (EM-1) a Graph-tick read sees the state the run just produced, never a pre-failure-phase state. Which Graph states count as "running" for a *lantern* is the Item DB's `lantern_on_states` (default `{0 OK, 1 DEGRADED}`, resolved 2026-10-26). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(orchestrator ruling: R22 as amended at the checkpoint (CP-3) — `emitter.place` declares the direct `after:` entry, so no read is ever lagged; the technical-director's proposal to sample slow inputs once per Graph run into canonical state is not adopted, because the direct ordering needs no sampled state and a restore at a Graph tick rebuilds the identical table.)*
219	
220	**EM-14 — Node lanterns are derived and switchless.** A NODE_LANTERN stands for the glow of a running machine (a pump, a reactor). It has no switch and makes no `set_load_request` call: `output_pm` is `⌊base_pm * term / 1000⌋` when the node is live and *running* (Formulas D.3 `node_lantern_output`), where `term` is the node's `run_pm` reading. A lantern gated on `served_pm` alone would glow from a switched-off machine (the same trap as EM-11), so the lantern reads a *running* quantity `run_pm` from the Graph read view — **delivered by the Graph** (LS-19 additions, 2026-10-27: `node(id).run_pm`, 0..1000 — 0 when the requested load is 0 (LOAD `req_w` 0, PUMP `throttle_pm` 0, REACTOR `out_w` 0), otherwise `served_pm` for a consumer and `⌊1000 × out_w / out_w_rated⌋` for a REACTOR; it is not the Graph's D.9 `duty_pm`, which reads 1000 for a machine switched off on a met tier and carries the same trap as EM-11). The Emitter **consumes `run_pm` as published and clamps it** to 0..1000 (D.3): it never recomputes it from `out_w`, so a REACTOR running above rated output cannot make a lantern outshine its `base_pm`, and a rated output of 0 is the Graph's guard, not an Emitter division. There is no fallback form: a browned-out or starved machine glows at its served fraction and a lantern that cannot read `run_pm` is a boot defect, not a weaker rule (a lantern at full `base_pm` while its machine starves would lie about power state, P1). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Lanterns are created and destroyed with their section (EM-5), counted against Lighting's lantern budget by authoring lint (EM-26), and killing the machine is the only way to dark one — "every loop you run is a lantern the web can see" (art bible Principle 3).

222	**EM-15 — Deployables and glowsticks: spawn on landing, steady, then waning, then gone.** `spawn_deployable(kind, pos_px, owner, life_ticks)` (E3) is called by Interaction's landing-tick hook (PC D.16: "the light exists only on landing"; the thrown light is never pre-played). The glowstick numbers are the Item DB's placeholders and are cited by name: `GLOWSTICK_LIFE_S` 150 (60–300), `GLOWSTICK_RADIUS_TILES` 2 (= 96 base px, 1.5–3), `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX` 4, `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM` 400, `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FLOOR_PM` 250 (Item DB IDB-12). No tick-denominated life constant is registered by this GDD: the record's `life_total_ticks` is `ticks_for_seconds(GLOWSTICK_LIFE_S)` = 9000 taken from the def at spawn, and the Item DB's rule that **the life is counted from the throw tick, not from landing** (a stick that never lands still burns out) is honoured by Interaction passing `life_ticks` = the life remaining at landing (9000 minus `THROW_ARC_TICKS` 30 for a thrown stick). This GDD owns the curve's *semantics*, id `WANE_LINEAR_25`: while the remaining life fraction is at or above `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM / 1000` the emitter holds its full reach (steady); below it, `reach_px` falls linearly (in the permille factor `f`, then floored to whole px) to `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FLOOR_PM / 1000` of full reach at the last tick (24 px at `life_remaining_ticks` 1); this is the Item DB's F-7 `reach_px(rem)` verbatim, so the two GDDs agree tick for tick; at `life_remaining_ticks` 0 the record is removed and its id retired (Formulas D.9). *(orchestrator ruling: the Item DB's steady-then-waning parameterisation, `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM` 400, is adopted over the routed ruling's linear-from-spawn curve — they are the same curve at `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM` 1000 — because the art bible specifies "steady at full value, then dimming monotonically", and the Item DB owns these numbers. A different number there is a conflict to surface, not a silent change.)* The output stays constant (`GLOWSTICK_BASE_PM`), the reveal radius shrinks, and that waning is **sim state**, not presentation, because it changes the real reveal radius (P1). It never flickers (art bible 3.2); the flicker of the VS-A flare, torch and decoy family is Lighting's and invisible to the query, which uses the steady mean. The stick lights the floor plane in ship-local px, counts as exposure like any pool (Attention may weight by area rather than radius — a pool at the floor radius has one sixteenth of the full area; the read view carries `reach_px` and the shape so either is derivable), and a stick landing in a closed room lights only that room (occluders). At most `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` non-evicting deployables exist. **Cap eviction is a visible wane, never an instant removal** *(creative-director CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 2: a light dying with no physical cause would break the promise that a stick's waning is its only clock, and would be a P1 lie)*: a spawn over the cap (Class B never rejects; the item was already spent, and Item DB rule (c): a landed stick is spent without refund) is applied in full, and the lowest-id deployable of the same kind that is not already evicting enters an **evict-wane** — `evict_tick` and `reach_at_evict` are written, its output stays `GLOWSTICK_BASE_PM`, and its reach falls linearly from its current reach to the 24 px floor over `ticks_for_seconds(GLOWSTICK_EVICT_WANE_S)` ticks (placeholder 10 s = 600 ticks, owner game-designer, Tuning Knobs), then the record is removed and its id retired (Formulas D.9b). It reads in the world as a stick guttering fast, the same visible monotone shrink as the ordinary wane, only quicker; the 24 px floor is the ordinary wane's own last value, so the final removal is the same event the ordinary end of life already is. An evicting stick still exposes, still gates actions and still sums at its current reach until it is gone; it does not count against `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE`, but the evicting tail is itself bounded by `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_EVICTING` (placeholder 4); an eviction that would exceed it completes the oldest evicting stick at once, increments `emitter_deployable_evict_overflow` and fires a debug assertion — a budget defect, never a gameplay state. **Eviction is meant to be unreachable by supply in the MVP, and that supply bound belongs to other owners** *(cross-GDD invariant I-SUPPLY, routed, Cross-References; the total glowsticks one seat carries across all stacks is at most `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE`, so no seat can have more sticks in flight than the cap)*: Suit & Equipment owns the per-seat carry count and start count, the Item DB owns `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX`, and Derelict Authoring owns the loose-stick supply by depth, which must not allow a throw-pickup-throw cycle to exceed the cap inside one `GLOWSTICK_LIFE_S` (a landed stick is never picked up again, Item DB rule (c), so a cycle needs a loose stick on the floor). The evict-wane exists because the bound can be violated by content and by VS-B (four seats × a stack of 4 is 16 against a cap of 8); every eviction increments the release telemetry counter `emitter_deployable_evictions`.

224	**EM-16 — The beacon is a pure function of time.** A BEACON is a 20° cone (shape row 8) whose axis is `beacon_aim = (beacon_phase + beacon_dir * ⌊T * AIM_UNITS / BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS⌋) mod 4096` with `T` the kernel clock tick (non-negative modulus), `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` 128 (2.13 s, inside the art bible's 2–3 s; placeholder, owner art-director / audio, confirmed by the Lighting spike), so the step is exactly 32 units per tick. Direction and phase are authored data; **no per-tick angle state exists**, which is what makes save-equivalence automatic (the kernel clock is persisted by the kernel). *(orchestrator ruling: the rational form of the systems-designer over the routed ruling's `T * BEACON_UNITS_PER_TICK`, because it is identical at 128 and lets any integer sweep length be valid — the ruled range 120–180 contained exactly one divisor of 4096.)* The beacon's brightness is the lamp formula when it carries a `node_ref` (MVP: it does — a dead ship's beacon is dark, P1), switched by `set_beacon`; turned on, it starts from the angle the pure function gives at that tick (no restart at phase 0). It is a dynamic-layer emitter (it rotates) and `gates_actions` is **false** *(orchestrator ruling: the systems-designer's F9 adopted, then **ruled kept by the user 2026-10-27 (Open Question 1, D20; no longer provisional)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* — a cone sweeping over a point lights it for 14 or 15 of every 128 ticks by phase (the cone is 456 units wide and the sweep advances 32 units per tick, so ⌊456/32⌋ = 14 or ⌈456/32⌉ = 15; about 11 %), and a prompt that strobes at the sweep rate, or a channel that aborts every 128 ticks, would be the system lying about what can be worked; the beacon exposes and is seen, it does not enable verbs. This narrows the Controller's PC-6 for one kind; routed to the technical-director and game-designer)*.

226	**EM-17 — Fault glow is a derived emitter kind.** FAULT_GLOW emitters stand for a venting ember, a power arc and cyan O₂ mist as point sources (art bible 2.8 / Failure & Trail). They are created and removed by `emitter.place` from the Graph's failure descriptors (`failures(filter)`), each keyed by `FailureDescriptor.mode` (a failure mode 1..10, or a descriptor-only id 20..26) plus `medium`, matching the Failure & Trail glow-table keys; the MVP rows with a glow are `1/FUEL`, `1/GAS`, `2`, `3`, `7`, `9`. For a descriptor that has a glow row: (1) `section_id` = the Graph's `section_of(descriptor.anchor)` — `section_of(node_id)` for a `(node_id, port_local_index)` anchor, `section_of(edge_id)` for an `edge_id` anchor (a compartment descriptor has no anchor and, by the F&T table, no glow row); for a `WALL_FACE` anchor it is the base of the host face, the first legal row in front of the wall (Layout LY-8 b), which already satisfies the clearance of EM-20 (b); and `origin_px` (derived) = `anchor_px + section_offset(section_id)` in the body frame, used for reach, distance and the occlusion start alike (EM-6: other kinds use their floor-plane anchor for both). `anchor_geometry` is a pure static read made once at creation and again in `post_restore`, never per tick. **Fallback when the Layout read is empty** (Layout returns nothing, without an error, only for a DISCARDED section, LY-23): no record is created on that Graph tick, `emitter_fault_glow_no_anchor` increments (release telemetry) and a debug assertion fires; reconciliation retries on the next Graph tick, and the case cannot persist for a loaded section because Layout's lint (`WALL_FITTING_NO_RUN`, AC-87) refuses a glow-capable fitting with no run. **Clearance lint, extended to every emitter anchor** (EM-20 b): a data-load lint checks the anchor of every authored FIXTURE, NODE_LANTERN and BEACON placement (the E1 input) and the head of every glow-capable `anchor_geometry` polyline against `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` for every `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rectangle, and refuses the build (`EMITTER_ANCHOR_CLEARANCE`, naming the placement or anchor); it covers template data, so no run-time nudge exists. If a defect gets past it, E1 or the FAULT_GLOW creation still makes the record (the exposure stays honest: `section_emission` counts it, P3) but increments `emitter_anchor_clearance_fail` and asserts in debug, and the emitter lights nothing in its own room (its segment starts inside a rectangle, so every pair is blocked) — a diagnosable defect, where the first draft's was silent. They are capped at `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` (placeholder 10); **a fault's light never goes dark with no physical cause** *(creative-director CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 1: a real failure whose light vanishes weakens P1, the physical consequence becomes invisible, and P2, a fault glow is one of the tells a careful player reads)*, so the cap is a content bound that is held by a boot invariant (I-CAPS (c), D.15: `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` is at least the most simultaneous glowing authored faults on one body plus a 25 % margin; in the MVP slice a welded body carries at most 6 simultaneous glow rows, so the floor is ⌈1.25 × 6⌉ = 8 ≤ 10, the 8 live faults being spread world-wide across bodies; registry: `mvp_fault_allocation`), and eviction is a last resort with three rules. (1) **Lowest severity first**: when reconciliation would hold more than `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` records, the records evicted are those with the lowest `sev`, ties broken by the higher descriptor id first (the kept set is the same as "highest `sev` wins, ties by ascending descriptor id"). (2) **A protected record is never evicted**: a record whose age `T − placed_tick` is below `ticks_for_seconds(W_MIN_WARNING_S)` (the Graph's registered fairness constant, 10 s = 600 ticks; cited, not restated) is protected, so the tell of a new fault is always shown for at least the Graph's warning window. (3) **Protection beats the cap**: if every candidate for eviction is protected, no record is evicted and the table stays over `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` (bounded only by `MAX_EMITTERS`, at which the creation rule of EM-24 refuses and counts), increments the release telemetry counter `emitter_fault_glow_overcap` and fires a debug assertion; it is trimmed back by rules 1 and 2 on the first Graph tick on which a candidate is no longer protected. Overcap is a content or budget defect and never a gameplay state. Every eviction increments `emitter_fault_glow_evictions`. An evicted glow removes only the descriptor's light and its exposure: the Failure & Trail emissive overlay on the sprite (an unshaded overlay, not an emitter) still draws the fault, so the fault stays visible in the world. **Timing (R22 as amended, CP-3):** `emitter.place` is `after: graph.propagate.failure`, so on a Graph tick it reads the descriptor list that run just produced and a glow appears on the Graph tick of its descriptor, never later; between Graph ticks the list cannot change. A FAULT_GLOW record is a normal record (it has an id from the canonical counter), so it persists as the set of descriptors it stood for. The emissive `_msk` trail glow on a sprite is an *unshaded overlay, not an emitter*, and exposes nothing: a lit-but-unregistered source would light a room Attention cannot see (Failure & Trail's brief). Whether a glow gates actions: yes (an arc lights the scrubber beside it). (Failure & Trail's designed FT-27 agrees: it supplies "a descriptor-to-glow data table (palette hex, radius in base px, flicker class bounded by FT-29)" and "Emitter State registers the emitter from the same descriptor". **Failure & Trail owns the glow-table rows including the ledger values `GLOW_BASE_PM[key]` and `SEV_GLOW_PM[0..4]` (placeholders it carries in V/A.6); this GDD owns D.11, the FAULT_GLOW record, `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` and `FAULT_GLOW_REACH_PX`, and multiplies the ledger values.** This GDD takes each row's `reach_px` from the F&T `radius_px` at the sev 4 column (the sev 3 column where sev 4 is n/a), defaulting to `FAULT_GLOW_REACH_PX` when a row carries none; a row radius outside [`REACH_MIN_PX`, `REACH_MAX_PX`] (invariant I-REACH, D.15) is a data defect — the data-load lint refuses it, and if one gets past the lint the record uses `FAULT_GLOW_REACH_PX`, `emitter_reach_invalid` increments and a debug assertion fires, so the glow is never dark and no division by a zero reach can occur. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* F&T's emissive layer "casts no light", which is the `_msk` sentence above.)

228	**EM-18 — The illumination model: contribution, curve classes, saturating sum.** For one emitter and one subject, the contribution `c` is **0** unless all of: the subject's `body_id` equals the emitter's (EM-30), the subject is inside the emitter's radius (`d2 <= reach_px²`, a closed edge), inside its cone for cone shapes (EM-19), not blocked (EM-20). The one exception is the owner's own beam on the owner's ACTOR subject, which contributes its apex value, facing- and occlusion-independent (EM-21). For every other pair `c = ⌊output_pm * f(d, reach_px) / 1000⌋` (Formulas D.7), `d` the exact integer floor of the distance from the emitter's origin (the chest, for the beam). Two **curve classes** are carried as a data table so the Lighting spike can replace a curve without changing the API: **SOFT** (pools, fixtures, glowsticks, lanterns, fault glow) `f = 1000 * (R - d) / R`, linear to zero at the fade-out radius; **HARD** (the cones and the beacon) `f = EDGE_FLOOR_PM + (1000 - EDGE_FLOOR_PM) * (R - d) / R`, so the contribution at the rim of a full-output hard-edged emitter is `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` (placeholder 250 permille, range 160–400, owner technical-artist, confirmed by the Lighting spike) and the lit boundary **is** the drawn hard edge. *(orchestrator ruling: this is a deliberate deviation from the routed ruling's single default curve `c = output_pm * (R - d) / R`, which contradicts its own "hard outer edge exactly at `reach_px`" clause: with `LIT_ON_PM` 150 a full-output wide beam of reach 288 px would be actionable only to `d <= 244` px — 44 px, almost a full tile, inside the hard edge the player sees, the light visibly falling on a valve the hand cannot reach, which is the game lying (P1) and contradicts art bible hero #1. Three specialists converged on the edge-floor remedy; rejected: lowering `LIT_ON_PM` toward 0 (a near-black pixel becomes actionable — a different lie, and hysteresis dies) and redefining the "drawn edge" as an iso-line at 150 permille (contradicts the hard edge). Surfaced as a deviation from the ruling's default in the return value, not a registry conflict.)* The consequence is intended: a *dimmed* hard-edged emitter (output below `⌈LIT_ON_PM * 1000 / EDGE_FLOOR_PM⌉` = 600) has an honestly smaller actionable area; a full-output emitter is actionable to its last pixel (invariant I-EDGE: `BEAM_BASE_PM * EDGE_FLOOR_PM >= 1000 * LIT_ON_PM`). For SOFT classes the actionable radius `r_lit` is **the largest `d` whose integer chain (D.7) gives `c ≥ LIT_ON_PM`**, published by the sim per emitter as `r_lit_px` (the closed form ⌊R × (output_pm − LIT_ON_PM) / output_pm⌋ of the first draft ran 1 px high for some dimmed outputs and is not used) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, inside the fade-out radius `reach_px` by design (a full fixture of reach 144 px is actionable to 122 px on approach). The **latch-release radius** `r_off_px` (the largest `d` whose chain gives `c ≥ LIT_OFF_PM`, D.7; 126 px for the same fixture) is where an already-lit subject stops being lit: Lighting draws a soft pool to the published `r_off_px` (a prompt never appears outside the visible pool), and `r_lit_px` is where an approaching subject first becomes actionable, `r_off_px − r_lit_px` px inside the drawn edge; the Lighting spike confirms the drawn edge (the art bible and Item DB "radius" numbers — 3 tiles, 2 tiles — are provisional, and the spike must decide whether they mean fade-out or readable radius). **Resolved 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix (G6): the pool is drawn to the latch-release radius (Lighting's `soft_pool_scale`, the registry source, wins); Emitter State's `lit` latch is unchanged.** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* **Aggregation is a saturating sum**, `lux_pm = min(1000, Σ c)`: integer addition is commutative, so no iteration-order dependence; several lamps in one room read brighter and expose more until fully lit. There is **no ambient term**: `AMBIENT_PM` is fixed at 0 in the sim, and Lighting's ambient is cosmetic and can never make an object actionable (P1; art bible Principle 1: unlit, not fogged). `lux_pm` sums every emitter (Horror reads it; Attention reads `emitters()` and never `lux_pm`, AT-4); `act_lux_pm` sums only the emitters whose `gates_actions` is true (EM-3) and feeds `lit` (EM-22).

230	**EM-19 — Cone membership is fixed-point and mirror-symmetric.** A cone test uses no trigonometry, square root or float at run time (Graph LS-1(b) precedent). Directions come from a table `DIR` of Q14 unit vectors — **the table is generated at build time by a data tool outside `src/sim/emitter/` and checked in as an integer data file, never computed in the sim module** (the boot step only loads it and asserts I-MIRROR and I-OVERFLOW, so the AC-2 lint holds) — indexed by an `AIM_UNITS` angle (0 = E, counter-clockwise, screen y down, so aim 3072 = S is `(0, +16384)`), generated from one quadrant by reflection so that `DIR[2048 - a] = (-ux, uy)` **exactly**. A subject at offset `r = anchor - origin` is in the cone iff `d2 <= R²`, `D > 0` and `D² >= d2 * COS2_Q28`, with `D = rx*ux + ry*uy` (Formulas D.5); the `D > 0` guard is required (the squared test alone accepts the opposite half-plane) and `d2 = 0` is inside every cone of that emitter, the apex included. The split beam is two tests at axes `aim ± 206` units; the wedge between them never closes (I-WEDGE), so a point is in at most one cone and its contribution is never doubled. Every product has a documented bound under 2^62 and the boot assertion refuses a build that violates it (Formulas D.15). The half-angles and the 18° offset are not integral in `AIM_UNITS`, so the shape table (EM-8) carries the encoded integers; the quantisation misplaces a rim by under 0.1° (under 0.7 px at 384 px), far inside the accepted committed-versus-drawn divergence. **The symmetry property is a test, not a hope**: the exposure of a mirrored scene (x → -x, aim `a` → `2048 - a`, `flip_h` toggled) equals the mirror image of the original exactly, for the five drawn and three mirrored facings, every `CHEST_POINT` animation row and all four shapes (Acceptance Criteria).

232	**EM-20 — Occlusion is integer geometry over the Layout's opaque footprints.** *(orchestrator ruling R3 — the one deliberate deviation from a routed thread's wording.)* The routed thread and the index describe occlusion as tests on "physics shapes". This GDD honours that in substance and changes the test method: the occluding shapes are the Layout's collision-footprint rectangles — walls (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24 base px: face 72, cap 24, tile 48), closed door leaves, and props flagged `occludes_light` — which are the very rectangles the Layout `PROJECTOR` hands to physics and `LocomotionStep` already sweeps the avatar's box against (PC-14, PC-18). The query tests a segment against those rectangles in exact integer arithmetic (Formulas D.6) behind an **`OccluderSource` seam** (`rects_in(aabb)`, ascending rect id; `version(section_id)`, a monotone counter bumped when any opaque rectangle in the section changes); there is **no physics backend in the MVP**, and one may exist only as a test cross-check (the hybrid option). The reasons that decide it: kernel H10 (systems stay scene-tree free, headless) and CR-13 G3 (the 2D physics engine makes no determinism claim, so a physics-derived `lit` flowing into a persisted block would be a physics observation that must be recorded for replay); a direct-space-state query is valid only during the physics step, while the kernel allows this query from presentation prompts at render rate, exactly the unsafe site; and the 2D ray API is not sourceable in the pinned engine reference (its `physics.md` carries only a 3D example). *Rules.* (a) **Cells are unit squares, boxes are closed, and the rule is conservative** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the first draft tested the closed span of cell *indices* `[x0, x1−1]`, which treats a cell as a point, so two abutting rectangles `[0,24)` and `[24,48)` left an open strip between x 23 and x 24 and an oblique ray crossed a wall seam untouched while Lighting drew a seamless shadow — a prompt lit behind a wall, a P1 lie; every worked example used an axis-aligned ray, which hid it)*: Layout's integer coordinates name pixel cells (LY-12 b), and a cell is a unit square centred on its integer coordinate. The box D.6 tests for an occupied span `(sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1)` returned by `rects_in` (= the stored `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)` as `(x0, y0, x1−1, y1−1)`) is the closed continuous box `[sx0 − ½, sx1 + ½] × [sy0 − ½, sy1 + ½]`, computed in **doubled coordinates** (every segment endpoint × 2) as the integer box `[2·sx0 − 1, 2·sx1 + 1] × [2·sy0 − 1, 2·sy1 + 1]` — in the stored rectangle's own terms `[2·x0 − 1, 2·x1 − 1] × [2·y0 − 1, 2·y1 − 1]`. Abutting rectangles share a box face (`[0,24)` and `[24,48)` give doubled x `[−1, 47]` and `[47, 95]`, touching at 47), so no wall seam, door-leaf/jamb joint or corner join leaves a strip; a segment that touches a box (a corner graze, an edge-on pass) is blocked; light does not leak around a corner. A segment endpoint is an integer cell, doubled to an even number against odd box bounds, so it is never exactly on a box face and is inside a box if and only if its cell is occupied. This convention is stated once, here and in D.6; Layout's occupied-span algebra (registry `rect_algebra_closed_span`, LY-12 b, D.2) remains the definition of *which cells are occupied* and of the anchor lint and is unchanged (routed to Layout: its rule text "the conservative closed test is applied to the occupied span" must read "the cell-unit box of the occupied span", Cross-References). (b) **Anchors must be at least `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` (1 base px) outside every occluding rectangle** (Chebyshev distance in cells from the occupied span, Layout D.2: a wall stored [408,432), whose occupied span is x 408..431, admits anchors at x = 407 and x = 432 and rejects 408 through 431; registry: `rect_algebra_closed_span`, the Layout's half-open convention), checked by authoring lint at registration. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **What the clearance means under the unit-square convention:** at 1 the anchor's centre is half a pixel (one doubled unit) outside the occluding box face, with its own cell directly adjacent to the wall, which guarantees that the segment's start is outside every box; a clearance of 0 would put the anchor inside the box. The check covers **every emitter anchor, not only subject anchors**: fixture, lantern and beacon placements at instantiate (a data-load lint) and FAULT_GLOW anchors at creation (EM-17); an emitter anchored on its own wall footprint would light nothing in its room and, in the first draft, raised no diagnostic. An anchor found strictly inside a footprint at run time is treated as blocked from every emitter (fails safe to dark) and increments `emitter_anchor_clearance_fail`. (c) **Actors and horrors never occlude.** A shadow with no occluder is a stage-2 sanity symptom (art bible 3.2 open item: it should not cast an occluding shadow) and must stay an unambiguous tell; so a horror standing in a beam leaves the beam unchanged and the subject beyond it lit. (d) **Door state is read from the Layout projection of the Graph's `door_state`** (Graph LS-6: the Graph owns door state and opening `area`) — the same door-leaf rectangle `collide` uses (PC-3, PC-18 test 7: same-tick door response) — so there is one source for collision and light, derived from the Graph in the same tick, and Emitter State holds **no door flag**. The door-leaf rectangle is the Layout's `door_leaf_gap` projection (Layout D.5, LY-9): `leaf_w` is continuous in the Graph's opening area and `leaf_w` 0 yields no rectangle, so no open-fraction threshold exists; `DOOR_LIGHT_OPEN_PM` is deprecated and unused. A hard-edged rim is a *step* (a full-output rim contributes `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` then 0 across one pixel), which the 150/120 hysteresis never sees; rim chatter while a beam sweeps is held by the Controller's committed-aim quantisation (`AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD` 32 units) and `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` (PC-6), and the hysteresis bites only for dimmed or soft light (brownout, waning glowsticks, fixture pools). Rejected alternative: rebuild every bit against `LIT_ON_PM` in `post_restore` (the earlier ruling R6) — a subject between the thresholds would flip from lit to unlit across a restore, `validate` at T+1 would accept in one run and reject `NOT_LIT` in the other, and canonical state downstream would diverge.)* Interaction's `validate` and the HUD prompt call this same `lit(ref)`, so the prompt never lies by omission (PC-6).

252	**EM-23 — The order of work inside `emitter.place`; static and dynamic layers; no subscriptions.** The hook does, in this order and nothing else: **W0** read upstream (`controller.state` and `body.state` for bound seats; the Layout `OccluderSource.version(section_id)`; the Graph's `served_pm` and `node(id)`; on Graph ticks the Graph's `failures(filter)`), and rewrite the derived `section_id` and `body_id` of each BEAM record and ACTOR subject from Body's `actor_section(actor_id)` and `body_of_actor(actor_id)` (a tick in which the foot crosses a door moves the beam's section in that tick) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, AND, for every loaded section whose Layout `static_version(section_id)` differs from the value cached at the last W0 (a derived per-section cache, never hashed, reset in `post_restore` so the first W0 after a restore re-reads everything), re-read `body_of(section_id)` and `section_offset(section_id)` and rewrite the derived `body_id` of every record and non-ACTOR subject whose `section_id` is that section (cost `W_FRAME` each, D.14); a change of `body_id` or `section_offset` is a FRAME CHANGE of that section *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; **W1** lifecycle (DEAD force-off, deployable aging, evict-wane (D.9b) and removal, `arm_tick` arming, fault-glow reconciliation); **W2** derive every emitter in ascending id (origin, aim, reach, `output_pm`, record `lit`); **W3** find the static-layer rows whose inputs changed; **W4** update them by deltas, in ascending (emitter id, subject ref), **synchronously — nothing is left pending past W4** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; **W5** the dynamic layer for every subject (with the owner-beam special case of EM-21: the owner's own beam adds its apex value to the owner's ACTOR `lux_pm` with no cone or occlusion test); **W6** saturating sums, hysteresis, write the subject table, record the tick's counted work; **W7** write dirty keys (EM-26). The **static layer** (FIXTURE, NODE_LANTERN, FAULT_GLOW, resting DEPLOYABLE) is cached as **per-pair contribution rows** `(emitter id, subject ref) → {d, f_pm, c}` (a row exists only while the emitter is in radius and unblocked) plus, per subject, an **unsaturated** raw sum `Σ c`, clamped to 1000 only when the answer is read. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The first draft cached a saturated partial sum, which is exact for *adding* an emitter (`min(1000, min(1000, a) + b) = min(1000, a + b)`) but cannot *remove* one (a saturated 1000 has forgotten what it summed), so every output change would have forced a full re-evaluation of the subject; with the pair rows every change is a delta: (i) an emitter's **output** changes (to or from 0, a brownout step, inrush): `c = ⌊output_pm × f_pm / 1000⌋` is recomputed from the stored `f_pm` with no geometry, and an `output_pm` of 0 stores `c` = 0 with no multiply while the rows (the geometry) are kept, so a blackout is a zeroing of rows and not a re-evaluation of the ship, and switching back on is a delta too; (ii) an emitter's integer **reach** changes (a waning stick): `d` and `f_pm` are recomputed for its rows and rows beyond the new reach are dropped, with no occlusion test (reach only shrinks, so no pair is added); (iii) an emitter is **created** (its candidate subjects are tested radius first, then occlusion, and rows are added) or **removed** (its rows are dropped); (iv) a subject is **registered or moved** (it is tested against the static emitters in range); (v) an **occluder** changes (only pairs whose segment bounding box meets the changed region are re-tested, below); (vi) the layer is **cold** (`post_restore`, section instantiate: everything is built); (vii) a **FRAME CHANGE** (a weld or cut, Layout LY-16 / LY-17) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Rows store `d`, `f_pm` and `c` and no coordinates, and a weld or cut moves a whole body by one translation (`rot_q` is 0 in the MVP, Layout D.6 / D.12), so: (a) rows whose emitter and subject lie in the same moved component are KEPT unchanged; (b) rows whose emitter `body_id` differs from the subject `body_id` after re-derivation are DROPPED (a cut: the rows that crossed the severed seam; cost `W_DELTA` each); (c) every subject with a changed `body_id` or on the host side of the seam is tested radius-first against the emitters of the OTHER side that are now on its body, and rows are ADDED (a weld; cost `U_sub` with the cross-seam counts of S8); (d) for each socket-host section the hatch slot set changed (PLATE <-> JAMB + LEAF), so pairs whose segment bounding box meets the changed region are re-tested exactly as for a leaf change (narrowing rule L / D). Layout reports the kind of change per section as `changed_region(section_id)` = ALL, REGION(box) or FRAME: FRAME = translation only, no re-test; REGION = the socket slot union box (a socket-host section that also moves reports REGION, and the Emitter detects its translation by comparing `section_offset(section_id)` with its cached value); ALL (build, discard, restore, or attach / detach if Layout declines REGION / FRAME) = cold rebuild of the affected bodies, priced as S8b. The rebuild stays synchronous (W3 / W4); nothing is pending past W4. Rows are derived, never hashed, rebuilt in ascending (emitter id, subject ref), and sized by ADR candidate 4; a row-table overflow changes cost, never an answer, and increments `emitter_pair_rows_overflow`; the **dynamic layer** (BEAM, BEACON, which rotate or translate every tick) is recomputed per tick with the cheapest rejects first — radius, then cone, then the occlusion test. A subject's static rows are updated when `emitter.place` *observes* a change in what it read last tick: the section's `OccluderSource.version(...)` changed, an emitter's `output_pm` or integer `reach_px` changed, an emitter was created or removed, or the subject moved. **Never by subscription**: kernel CR-10 ("simulation systems never subscribe; sim-to-sim is ordered step reads or commands"); dirty keys are the notification channel for PRESENTATION and friends, not an input to this block. A pose-unchanged skip (a dynamic emitter whose origin, aim, output, shape and occlusion origin equal last tick's skips re-evaluation) is a pure optimisation and changes no answer. A static emitter's cost is paid when something changes, not every tick; a glowstick's reach steps by one px every 50 ticks while it wanes (3600 ticks over 72 px, D.9), so the rows of the subjects in its range are recomputed that often (D.14, S5). **Narrowing rule for door leaves** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `OccluderSource.version(section_id)` says only *that* something in the section changed, and a leaf bump arrives at the Graph's step rate while a door travels (roughly ten per second), so a response that re-tests every pair of the section would cost 11,522 units per bump (D.14, S1: 14 × `T_sub` 823) against `B` 10,000 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The Emitter therefore re-tests only pairs whose segment bounding box meets the changed region: **(L)** Layout publishes the changed region with the bump (ask E-N, a union box of the old and new leaf rectangles; a structural bump — build, discard, restore — reports `ALL`; attach and detach report REGION / FRAME (trigger vii) when Layout supplies them, else `ALL`), or, if Layout declines, **(D)** every pair whose segment bounding box meets a door-leaf pre-filter box of its section is tagged *dynamic* and evaluated every tick in the dynamic layer, which costs the same amount every tick instead of once per bump (priced in S1). ADR candidate 4 chooses between L and D on Layout's answer; both fit the budget. A restore-time bump (Layout's `post_restore`, version 1 to 2) is treated as a leaf-region change over that section's leaf boxes, not as `ALL`, because structural geometry is valid straight after `restore()` (Layout LY-26 b). **The contract is "never stale", and the rebuild is synchronous** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; resolves the question that D.13's age bound left open)*: W3 and W4 finish every update inside the tick, before W6 writes the table, so there is no pending state and the D.13 bound (age 0 or 1 tick) holds for every reader, including Interaction's `validate` at T−1 and its six-tick re-check, Attention and Horror. A tick whose updates exceed the ceiling of D.14 still completes them, increments `emitter_rebuild_over_ceiling` and is a hitch to be removed by content or by the ordered fallbacks, never deferred. **Alternative (b), rejected and recorded for ADR candidate 4:** a deterministic counted-unit cap per tick, a widened staleness bound and a fail-safe lit-or-dark rule for pending subjects. It was rejected because (1) `lit` would then depend on a rebuild queue that is derived, not canonical, so a snapshot restored mid-queue (which rebuilds cold and complete) would answer differently from the uninterrupted run — kernel G4 broken in exactly the way the old probe budget broke it (EM-24); (2) a fail-safe-dark rule would blink the prompts of a whole room on every door bump; and (3) it would rewrite the age bound that three designed GDDs already build on. The ceiling's named owner is the technical-director; the exposure spike reports it (AC-53).

254	**EM-24 — Counted work, not wall-clock; the caps.** The per-tick exposure cost is bounded by **counted work units**, never by timing — a time-based governor would be nondeterministic. The caps (all *placeholder, owner technical-director, confirmed by the exposure spike and the Interaction / Derelict Authoring content counts*; never inherited from a default of 64): `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` 192 (derived from the MVP slice's 14 compartments — home-ship 5, derelict A 4, derelict B 5 — their verb-bearing nodes, doors counted twice for their two face subjects, loose items, actors and horror subjects; Formulas D.14; *orchestrator pick: the systems-designer's 192 over the technical-director's 128, because doors register two subjects (EM-20 e) and the MVP Graph's node count supports a larger interactable set*), `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS` 16 (the 17th moving registration returns false, increments `emitter_moving_overflow` and the subject reads dark, the same fail-safe as `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS`), `MAX_EMITTERS` 96, `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` 8, `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_EVICTING` 4, `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` 10. **The caps are content budgets, held at data load, not gameplay states** *(CD-GDD-ALIGN concerns 1 and 3)*: the MVP slice has exactly 8 live faults world-wide, of which a welded body carries at most 6 simultaneous glow rows (registry `mvp_fault_allocation`); I-CAPS therefore requires `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` to be at least the most simultaneous glowing authored faults on one body plus 25 % (⌈1.25 × 6⌉ = 8; the cap of 10 keeps 2 of headroom), and requires the **dynamic registrants** that arrive after boot to be held to per-category budgets owned by their authors: Derelict Authoring owns the budget for authored OBJECT and ITEM subjects and for dropped loot and spawned salvage per section, Horror Entities owns the horror-subject budget (`HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` 2 (Horror Entities, registry), all moving; Horror's `horror_subject_count` holds `HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` + `A_max` 4 = 6 ≤ `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS`) and the share of `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS` it may use, Interaction owns the dropped-item registrations, and the deployable budget is `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` + `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_EVICTING` (D.14, D.15 I-CAPS (d)). A runtime overflow of any cap is a defect of one of those budgets, is counted by a release-build telemetry counter (`emitter_subjects_overflow`, `emitter_moving_overflow`, `emitter_fault_glow_overcap`, `emitter_fault_glow_evictions`, `emitter_deployable_evictions`, `emitter_deployable_evict_overflow`, and, added by the 2026-10-27 design review, `emitter_create_refused`, `emitter_fault_glow_no_anchor`, `emitter_anchor_clearance_fail`, `emitter_reach_invalid`, `emitter_actor_section_none`, `emitter_pair_rows_overflow`, `emitter_rebuild_over_ceiling`, and, added by the re-review, `emitter_dock_status_missing`, `emitter_invalid_transition` and the playtest counters of the metric stub) as well as asserted in debug, and is never something a design relies on. `EXPOSURE_BUDGET_MS` is **0.4 ms P99** for `emitter.place` plus all exposure evaluation (placeholder, spike on the release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, delegated ruling R12; the kernel's `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 is a logging threshold and P3's target is ≤ 2.0 ms P99 with the Graph at 0.5 ms and Controller + Body about 0.3 ms). It is the *steady-state* budget; the named rare-event scenarios of D.14 are held to `EXPOSURE_TICK_CEILING_MS` (hot class) and `COLD_REBUILD_CEILING_MS` (cold class), both owned by the technical-director. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Mandatory work (the dynamic layer, static rebuilds, the subject table) is never skipped. **Creation at `MAX_EMITTERS`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the first draft had no run-time rule at the global cap)*: when the record count equals `MAX_EMITTERS` a creation is **refused**, never made by removing a light that has a physical cause. E1 refuses the section's remaining records, `spawn_deployable` returns false (the item was already spent, Item DB rule (c)), and a FAULT_GLOW reconciliation creates nothing for the lowest-ranked descriptors; each refusal increments `emitter_create_refused` (release telemetry, per kind) and asserts in debug. Within one pass creations are admitted in `priority` order, highest first (BEAM 255, BEACON 200, FIXTURE 120, DEPLOYABLE 100, FAULT_GLOW 80, NODE_LANTERN 60; ties by ascending creation order), so the light the player most needs is the one kept; the seat beams are never refused, because their slots are reserved (I-CAPS (a) counts the bound seats). The cap is a content budget held by I-CAPS (a); the rule exists so that a breach is deterministic, counted and visible, never a gameplay state. **Probes and `lit_by(point)` are deferred to Vertical Slice A** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: no MVP consumer calls them (Horror HE-19 and HE-25 use Layout `room_at` / `room_adjacency` and make no `probe()` call, Attention AT-4 makes none, Sanity no longer uses `lit_static` (deferred to VS-A, EM-25), and Interaction's re-checks are `lit(ref)` lookups), so `probe`, `lit_by`, `MAX_PROBES_PER_TICK`, `W_PROBE`, `probes_allowed` and the probe counter are removed from the MVP read view, budget and acceptance criteria. The first draft derived `probes_allowed` from the previous tick's counted work `T_mand_prev`, which depends on cache hits and skips, is not canonical (absent from EM-28) and is rebuilt differently after `post_restore`, so the same probe could answer OK in a live run and `UNKNOWN` after a restore — a kernel G4 break that the old AC-54 could not detect. **Reserved for VS-A:** if probes return, their budget is a *constant* number per tick that is never derived from counted work, and their signatures take the frame, `probe(body_id, point)` and `lit_by(body_id, point)`, because geometry is compared only within one body (EM-30). The GDScript op cost is not sourceable from the pinned engine reference (no scripting module), so every cost number is a model parameter for the spike; the fallback if the dynamic layer is too slow is a baked per-room illumination grid for the static layer (the brief's option c), then reducing `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS`, then room-gated broadphase (the numeric decision table of D.14 governs the order). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*

256	**EM-25 — Query semantics, the read view and the staleness bound.** Public reads are table lookups against the subject table and the emitter records; they are pure, side-effect free and callable from `validate`, from P3 and from presentation prompts, **never from notification handlers that decide state** (kernel C.3 row 7). Because `emitter.place` runs every tick, a reader that does not declare `after: [emitter.place]` sees a value **at most one tick old**; P2 `validate` sees the table committed by tick T-1's `emitter.place`; a hook that declares `after: [emitter.place]` sees the current tick (the routed ruling's correction of the brief's "up to 5 ticks", which was borrowed from the Graph's divisor-6 caveat and does not apply to a divisor-1 hook). Source ages stack on top and are named, not hidden: the beam's committed aim is up to the Controller's tolerance behind the drawn aim; a lamp's brightness follows `served_pm`, which changes only on Graph ticks. Owners of channelled verbs re-check exposure every 6 ticks through the same `lit(ref)` and abort if unlit at a check (PC-7); a single-tick flicker between checks is tolerated. Attention declares `after: [graph.propagate.power, emitter.place]` (cross-divisor `after:` is already in use: `controller.step` is `after: suit.vitals`) and Horror Entities declares `after` both Attention and `emitter.place` (kernel row 9; HE-3), so the former asks are met and AC-60 lints them. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

447	### D.2b Switch commit spacing *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D32; default applied, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20))*
448	
449	The `switch_commit_spacing` formula is defined as:
450	
451	`accept ⇔ last_toggle_tick < 0 ∨ commit_tick − last_toggle_tick ≥ SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS`, with `commit_tick = T_a` for a beam toggle, for an OFF that darkens a lit or armed lamp, and for **every switch of a self-powered `node_ref` 0 fixture** (no M14 call, no ARMING, `armed` always 1: its ON commits at the apply tick, so charging it the `arm_tick` of D.2 would shift its spacing check by 0..5 ticks *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), `commit_tick = arm_tick` (D.2) for the ON of a Graph-powered lamp, and no test at all for an OFF applied while the lamp is ARMING (it cancels an ON that never became visible); a rejection is `TOO_SOON` for `toggle_beam` and `COOLDOWN` for `set_switch`
452	
453	**Variables:**
454	
455	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
456	|---|---|---|---|---|
457	| `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` | int | 12 (11–20) | this GDD, placeholder owner technical-director and technical-artist, confirmed by 2D Lighting LO-22 | the least number of commit ticks between two realised switch transitions of one emitter |
458	| `last_toggle_tick` | int | −1 or ≥ 1 | the record (EM-4) | commit tick of the previous realised transition |
459	| `commit_tick` | int | `T_a`..`T_a` + 5 | D.2 | the projected tick at which the requested transition becomes visible (`T_a` exactly for a self-powered fixture) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
460	| `N(s)` | int | — | derived | the most realised transitions of one emitter inside any rolling window of 60 ticks at spacing `s` |
461	
462	**Derivation (the constraint `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` satisfies).** The flash budget is `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3 per second, and the registry `flash_count` unit is ⌈n / 2⌉ (X9), so one emitter may realise at most N = 6 transitions in any rolling second (⌈6 / 2⌉ = 3; seven would be four flashes). At spacing `s`, a half-open window of 60 ticks holds at most N(s) = ⌈60 / s⌉ transitions (2D Lighting's governor convention) and a window closed at both ends holds at most ⌊60 / s⌋ + 1. Requiring N ≤ 6: half-open gives 60 / s ≤ 6, `s` ≥ 10; closed gives ⌊60 / s⌋ ≤ 5, `s` ≥ 11. `s` = 12 ships because it satisfies both with a transition of margin under the governor's count (N(12) = 5, ⌈5 / 2⌉ = 3 flashes; the closed count is 6, three flashes) and because it equals Interaction's `TAP_REARM_TICKS` 12. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the first draft added "so a player's tap path is rarely the tighter guard". That is false for ON-then-OFF: the tap guard spaces submissions and this guard spaces commits, so the fastest legal OFF after an ON is refused in 5 of the 6 latency alignments, see the table below.)* Upper limit: above 20 ticks (0.33 s) a deliberate double tap reads as a dropped press; hence the range 11–20.
463	
464	**Output Range:** accept or reject; at most 5 realised transitions of one emitter in any 60 ticks, hence at most 3 flashes. **Examples (fixture, previous realised OFF at tick 120):** an ON requested at `T_a` 121 has `arm_tick` 126 (D.2: 121 mod 6 = 1, +5) and 126 − 120 = 6 < 12 → `COOLDOWN`; at `T_a` 126 (a Graph tick) `arm_tick` 126 → 6 → `COOLDOWN`; at `T_a` 127 `arm_tick` 132 → 12 → accepted; at 132 `arm_tick` 132 → accepted. **ON then OFF:** ON at 1201 (`arm_tick` 1206, realised at 1206, so `last_toggle_tick` 1206 from then); OFF at 1203 → cancels, accepted, writes nothing; but OFF at 1213 → 1213 − 1206 = 7 → `COOLDOWN`, OFF at 1218 → 12 → accepted. **Beam:** toggles submitted on 60 consecutive ticks T..T + 59 are accepted at T, T + 12, T + 24, T + 36, T + 48, which is 5 accepted and 55 rejected `TOO_SOON` (AC-90). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
465	
466	**ON then the fastest legal OFF (the `12 − L` table)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: an ON applied at `T_a` commits at `arm_tick` = `T_a` + `L` (`L` = D.2, 0..5). The player's next tap may be applied `TAP_REARM_TICKS` 12 later, at `T_a` + 12, and commits at once. The gap between the two commits is 12 − `L`, so the OFF is refused `COOLDOWN` whenever 12 − `L` < `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` 12, that is whenever `L` > 0, and is accepted only when `L` = 0.
467	
468	| `T_a mod 6` | `L` | ON commits | fastest OFF applies / commits | gap 12 − `L` | OFF result |
469	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
470	| 0 | 0 | `T_a` | `T_a` + 12 | 12 | accepted |
471	| 1 | 5 | `T_a` + 5 | `T_a` + 12 | 7 | `COOLDOWN` |
472	| 2 | 4 | `T_a` + 4 | `T_a` + 12 | 8 | `COOLDOWN` |
473	| 3 | 3 | `T_a` + 3 | `T_a` + 12 | 9 | `COOLDOWN` |
474	| 4 | 2 | `T_a` + 2 | `T_a` + 12 | 10 | `COOLDOWN` |
475	| 5 | 1 | `T_a` + 1 | `T_a` + 12 | 11 | `COOLDOWN` |
476	
477	At the sim a refusal is a domain code (`COOLDOWN`, no HUD text, no light change), so a deliberate off-tap right after an on-tap is refused in 5 of 6 alignments (a tap `L` ticks later, 1 to 5, gets through). The creative-director reads a silently ignored deliberate tap as a broken switch that erodes trust in the light model, which the horror depends on. **Options (resolved 2026-10-28, delegated ruling R20, Open Question 31):** (a) raise the ON-to-OFF tap re-arm to 17 (`SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` 12 + the worst `L` 5), so every tap that gets through commits at least 12 after the ON and none is silently dropped (a sibling change, Interaction's `TAP_REARM_TICKS`); (b) keep 12 and add a readable refusal tell (a short dull switch-resistance cue, presentation only, no HUD text, never a light change); (c) keep 12 and silent. **Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling G2 (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): the creative-director's stated lean is against a silent refusal, so (b) is the applied default:** the `COOLDOWN` result reaches the submitter as its terminal result and Interaction's existing failed-action cue path (the path that already carries `NOT_LIT`; the Adapter already plays `cue_input_ignored` for a `toggle_beam` inside the rate-limit window) plays one short dull cue for it, with no light change and no HUD text; the sim, the value 12 and every formula are untouched, so nothing reverses; (a) is not adopted (Open Question 31, resolved 2026-10-28, delegated ruling R20). The cue itself is Interaction's and the Presenter's to draw (a cross-GDD note). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*

779	## Edge Cases
780	
781	**Switching, power and lamps**
782	
783	- **If `set_switch` applies on a Graph tick (`T mod 6 = 0`)**: the lamp is lit by that tick's `emitter.place`; on any other tick it is lit at the next multiple of 6, at most 5 ticks later (D.2). One latency story, no hidden term.
784	- **If a switched-on lamp's `served_pm` is 0 (brownout to zero, SCRAM, shed)**: the lamp is STARVED, `output_pm` 0, `switch_on` unchanged and its request still queued; it lights again with no new command when power returns.
785	- **If a lamp's `output_pm` is at or below `LIT_ON_PM` (a deep brownout, or the 150 permille pump lantern)**: it lights nothing but its own anchor, still adds to sums, and Lighting draws it dim; an honest dim, never a prompt.
786	- **If a lamp's node is SALVAGED, ABSENT, dormant or tombstoned (not structurally present)**: M14 is a no-op, `live` is false, `output_pm` is 0, a `SYSTEM`-origin `set_switch` or `set_beacon` is rejected `NOT_LIVE`, a `PLAYER`-origin `set_switch` is accepted and flips `switch_on` (IA-11(a): no node read, no oracle) and the lamp stays dark, and the record stays until its section is discarded. A FAILED or DESTROYED node is different: both origins are accepted (next bullet). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
787	- **If a lamp's node goes FAILED or DESTROYED**: `output_pm` is 0 on that Graph tick (the hook is after the failure phase); `switch_on` is retained, so a repair re-lights the lamp without a command. A `set_switch` of either origin on such a node is accepted (it is structurally present, EM-7) and goes STARVED. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
788	- **If eight lamps are switched on in one tick on a marginal island**: all read the same inrush dip of `served_pm` for `INRUSH_STEPS` runs (945 in the D.2 example); ascending-id application makes the result order-free.
789	- **If a lamp is switched off while ARMING**: `switch_on` is false at once, M14 `(node_ref, 0)` is queued and the lamp is never lit; the pending `arm_tick` is discarded.
790	- **If `set_switch` targets a non-FIXTURE (a lantern, the beam)**: rejected `NOT_SWITCHABLE`; no state change and no M14 call.
791	- **If a FIXTURE has `node_ref` 0 and is neither the declared cryo-bay emergency lamp nor a dock room's DOCK_STATUS glow**: the authoring lint and boot refuse it (`SELF_POWERED_LAMP_COUNT`); the declared lamps are armed always, fixed `base_pm`, no M14 (Derelict Authoring is designed: DA-23 declares `fixture_subkind_emergency`). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; DOCK_STATUS added 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2)*
792	- **If a dock room has no DOCK_STATUS glow, or two**: the authoring lint refuses it (exactly one per dock room, Derelict Authoring's rule); at run time the pod console would read unlit and `pod_hop` would refuse `NOT_LIT`, which the lint exists to make unreachable. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2)*
793	- **If the pod leaves a dock or parks at one**: Web Map's apply that writes `pod_at` calls E10 off for the dock it leaves and on for the dock it parks at; the glow changes with no ARMING and no commit-spacing guard, so there is no `COOLDOWN` to retry and no case in which a refused call leaves the glow lit over an empty cradle; a call for an unknown section, or one with no glow, is a no-op returning false and counts `emitter_dock_status_missing` (a defect the authoring lint exists to prevent). At `init_world` the home dock's glow is on after step 7 and the derelict docks' glows are off.  *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2, D32)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
794	- **If a lamp is toggled again inside `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` of its last realised transition**: the command is rejected `COOLDOWN` (a beam `TOO_SOON`), `switch_on` is unchanged and nothing is lit or darkened; an OFF during ARMING is exempt and cancels (D.2b). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D32)*
795	- **If a lantern's machine is switched off (requested load 0) or starved (breaker open, or served below its request)**: output follows the Graph's `run_pm` clamped to 0..1000 — 0 for a switched-off machine, `base_pm × the served fraction` for a starved or browned-out one; there is no fallback form (D.3). **If a REACTOR reports `run_pm` above 1000** (output above rated): the clamp holds the lantern at `base_pm`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
796	
797	**Beam and pose**
798	
799	- **If `toggle_beam` applies**: `switch_on` flips and the beam is lit on the apply tick; a turn-ON at zero charge is rejected `CHARGE_EMPTY` and the light does not change (the pre-played click is the Presenter's).
800	- **If charge reaches zero mid-channel**: Suit's `force_off` lands before the same tick's `emitter.place`; the owner's 6-tick re-check then finds the target unlit and aborts, so at most five ticks of channel run on a dark target.
801	- **If the actor is DOWNED**: the beam keeps its committed state, aim frozen at the last committed value, origin from the down row's `chest_sim`; a downed crewmate is a locator. **If DEAD**: forced off at that tick, unobservable in the MVP because the death stub restarts from the last autosave at that tick's P6.
802	- **If the actor is STAGGERED**: the beam is unchanged and `toggle_beam` is rejected `NOT_ACTIONABLE` (a defensive double of the Controller's input-ignore).
803	- **If the player runs with aim different from facing**: the beam follows the committed aim; the split axes are ±206 units off aim, not facing.
804	- **If an interactable lies between the chest and the feet in screen-y while the player faces up-screen**: it is behind the apex, unlit and unprompted unless it lies within the foot spill: the sim adds no hidden compensation beyond the ruled spill (EM-6). `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` ships at 24 (user ruling D24, 2026-10-27; Open Question 17), so an item within 18 px of the feet is lit and prompts while the beam is on, an item a full tile (48 px) to the side is not, and with the beam off there is no spill; AC-10b tests the ruled default and the spill-off boundary. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
805	- **If the feet stand 1–44 px south of the first legal row in front of a north wall** (the band over all `CHEST_POINT` rows: `h − 24 ≤ s ≤ h − 1`, 10–33 px for the walk row): the chest point is inside the footprint, the apex stays at the chest, and the occluder segment starts at the foot, so a north-aimed beam is blocked at once and a south-aimed beam is unaffected; whether Lighting draws the same (a beam that rendered black here would be a P1 lie) is AC-57 and the pre-implementation gate of EM-6. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
806	- **If the avatar is mirrored (`flip_h`)**: `chest_sim.x` moves by up to 4 px and the cones are recomputed from the new apex in the same tick; a mirrored scene yields the exact mirror image of every `lux_pm` and `lit` (I-MIRROR).
807	- **If any animation row changes the chest point (run lean, carry, work, stagger, down)**: the apex moves by the data delta in the same tick with no smoothing.
808	- **If the mouse flicks the aim**: the committed aim lags the drawn aim by up to 2.8° and 3 ticks; a subject in that sliver may disagree with the drawn edge for up to 3 ticks, tolerated by the 6-tick re-check.
809	- **If a subject lies in the split beam's dark wedge**: it is in neither cone and contributes 0 at every aim (the wedge is at least 16° and never closes); dead ahead of a split beam is dark, by design.
810	- **If a subject is exactly on the hard edge (`d2 = R²`) or exactly on a cone boundary ray**: it is inside (the edge is closed and the cone test is `≥`); one pixel farther it is outside. **If a subject is at the apex (`d2 = 0`)**: it is inside every cone of that emitter.
811	- **If the owner is alone with the lamp on**: the owner's ACTOR `lux_pm` is the beam's full `output_pm` (1000), facing- and occlusion-independent, so Horror sees a lit player and Attention counts the beam once from the emitter list; the owner's `act_lux_pm` gains nothing and Attention must not add the beam again.
812	- **If `bind_beam` changes the shape**: it takes effect at the next `emitter.place`; there is no input for it, and a shape change is a loadout event.
813	
814	**Occlusion, queries and caps**
815	
816	- **If a segment only touches a rectangle (corner graze), crosses a seam between abutting rectangles (wall run, door-leaf/jamb joint) or passes through a corner shared by two diagonal rectangles**: it is blocked, because cells are unit squares and abutting boxes share a face (EM-20 a, D.6); an oblique ray never slips through a seam. An anchor within `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` of a footprint fails the registration lint, and an anchor found strictly inside a footprint at run time is blocked from every emitter and reads dark. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
817	- **If a door closes mid-channel**: the next `emitter.place` observes the `OccluderSource.version(section_id)` change, rebuilds the static layer for the section, the target reads dark and the owner's re-check aborts the channel within 6 ticks.
818	- **If a door is partly open**: the door-leaf rectangle is the Layout's `door_leaf_gap` projection (`leaf_w` continuous in the Graph's opening area; `leaf_w` 0 yields no rectangle), so light passes exactly the gap the leaf leaves; `DOOR_LIGHT_OPEN_PM` is deprecated and unused.
819	- **If a horror or an actor stands between an emitter and a subject**: nothing is occluded and the subject beyond stays lit; a shadow with no occluder is a stage-2 symptom and must stay an unambiguous tell.
820	- **If a carried item is dropped**: it re-registers as a static ITEM subject at the drop anchor and is evaluated at the next `emitter.place` (it was unregistered at pickup, EM-21).
821	- **If the subject is an unregistered ref (including a Perception Filter phantom target)**: `lux` 0 and `lit` false, indistinguishable from a registered unlit subject in release, so the query is no existence oracle; `registered(ref)` exists in debug builds only.
822	- **If registrations exceed `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS`, or moving registrations exceed `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS`**: `register_subject` returns false, `emitter_subjects_overflow` (or `emitter_moving_overflow`) increments in release builds as telemetry, the subject reads dark (fails safe) and a debug assertion fires. **This is a content or budget bug and never a gameplay state**: a real object inside a beam that refuses to prompt would break the honest edge (design test 1) and read as a hallucination (the P4 "reach for it" falsifier), so the per-category budgets (Derelict Authoring: authored objects, items, dropped loot and spawned salvage; Horror Entities: horror subjects; Interaction: dropped items) are held by I-CAPS (d), a breach seen in telemetry is fixed in the owning budget, and no design may rely on the refusal. **If a source calls `probe()` or `lit_by()` in the MVP**: the lint fails the build (EM-24; both are deferred to VS-A). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
823	- **If a subject's `body_id` differs from an emitter's (an unwelded section, a section cut off, a pod)**: that emitter contributes 0 (EM-30); cross-body light between unwelded bodies is a Ship Body question for VS-A. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
824	- **If a weld joins two bodies (the MVP home+B weld)**: in the tick the weld applies every record and subject of the absorbed body re-derives to the surviving (lower-id) body (EM-4, EM-23 W0); the beam and ACTOR (already on the home body via Body) now light B's objects, and B's fixtures, lanterns, glowsticks, fault glows and objects count toward the player; the new hatch leaf starts closed (`leaf_w` = `width_px`, LY-16), so the hatch blocks light until the opening area is > 0 and no light leaks through a closed leaf. **If a cut separates them**: records and subjects of the new component re-derive to the new `body_id`, the cross-seam rows are dropped in the same tick, and objects that were lit across the seam go dark that tick (hysteresis: `act_lux_pm` 0 < `LIT_OFF_PM` 120). A glowstick in a cut-off section keeps its section and follows its section's body. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
825	- **If in-view emitters exceed Lighting's budget (24 non-shadow + 6 shadow, 8 lanterns)**: the sim never culls by view, a cut light still exposes (P3), a debug assertion reports it and `priority` makes Lighting's cut reproducible; the authoring lint should have refused the content.
826	
827	**Deployables, beacon and fault glow**
828	
829	- **If a glowstick lands on a dormant or unknown section**: `spawn_deployable` is a no-op returning false, Interaction has already spent the item and no light ever existed. **If it lands inside a closed room**: it lights that room only (the walls occlude).
830	- **If two glowsticks overlap**: contributions saturate at 1000 and each wanes on its own clock. **If a spawn exceeds `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE`**: the new stick spawns in full (Class B never rejects) and the lowest-id non-evicting deployable of the same kind enters a visible evict-wane (D.9b): its reach falls from where it is to 24 px over `GLOWSTICK_EVICT_WANE_S` (10 s) and only then is it removed, so no light dies with no physical cause; `emitter_deployable_evictions` increments. **If an eviction would exceed `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_EVICTING`**: the oldest evicting stick completes at once, `emitter_deployable_evict_overflow` increments and a debug assertion fires (a budget defect, I-SUPPLY). **If a section is discarded with live deployables**: they are removed with it.
831	- **If `life_remaining_ticks` reaches 0**: the record is removed that tick and its id retired, the subjects it lit re-read next tick, and there is no fade (the waning already took the reach to 24 px).
832	- **If `set_beacon` turns the beacon on**: it starts from the angle the pure function gives at that tick, not phase 0; off, it contributes 0 from the next tick. **If its bus is dead**: `output_pm` is 0 (D.1) while the aim stays a pure function of `T`.
833	- **If the beacon sweeps a subject in an otherwise dark room**: `lux_pm` is above 0 for 14 or 15 of every 128 ticks (by phase; the same count in two runs and across a restore) and `lit` stays false, so no prompt strobes and no channel aborts at the sweep rate.
834	- **If more than `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` descriptors have glow rows**: the unprotected records with the lowest `sev` (ties: the higher descriptor id first) are evicted and `emitter_fault_glow_evictions` increments; a record younger than `ticks_for_seconds(W_MIN_WARNING_S)` (600 ticks) is never evicted, and if every candidate is protected nothing is evicted, the table stays over the cap, `emitter_fault_glow_overcap` increments and a debug assertion fires, with the table trimmed on the first Graph tick that has an unprotected candidate. The MVP slice does not reach the cap: a welded body carries at most 6 simultaneous glow rows of the 8 live faults (registry `mvp_fault_allocation`), and 10 ≥ ⌈1.25 × 6⌉ = 8 (I-CAPS (c)). An evicted glow removes only the light and exposure; the Failure & Trail overlay on the sprite still shows the fault. **If a descriptor's `sev` falls to 0 or its `intensity_pm` ends**: the record is removed on that Graph tick.
835	- **If a long-aged fault (a SCRAM held for minutes) keeps its descriptor while Failure & Trail's overlay decays** (Derelict Authoring OQ-V3): the FAULT_GLOW `output_pm` follows the descriptor's `sev` alone (D.11) and never the overlay's age; overlay decay is Failure & Trail's presentation and changes neither `output_pm` nor exposure, so a glow that should fade with age must be expressed by F&T as a falling `sev` or `intensity_pm`.
836	- **If a `mod_lamp` sits on the lowest `power_tier`** (Derelict Authoring OQ-V4): its output is `base_pm × served_pm / 1000` (D.1); the lowest tier is the first shed under a shortfall, so it reads dimmer only while its tier is under-served (`served_pm` < 1000) and identical to any other lamp at full supply; whether a given `served_pm` reads *visibly* dimmer is the Lighting spike's to confirm.
837	- **If a sprite carries an emissive `_msk` trail glow**: it is an unshaded overlay, not an emitter, and exposes nothing.
838	
839	**Save, restore, boot and co-op**
840	
841	- **If a game is restored with a subject between `LIT_OFF_PM` and `LIT_ON_PM`**: its `lit` bit is canonical and kept, so `validate` at T+1 reads the same answer as in the uninterrupted run (kernel G4).
842	- **If a save is taken at a Graph tick and restored**: the Graph's `post_restore` rebuilds `served_pm` and the descriptor list, so the subject table and every lamp `output_pm` match uninterrupted play at the next five ticks; the Graph now does so (LS-21 and its restore edge case, 2026-10-27), and AC-41 fails if a regression removes the rebuild (lamps would read dark for up to 5 ticks). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
843	- **If a restore completes (the kernel binding table is rebuilt)**: the kernel's LOADING rebuild re-binds the seat beams from `beam_bindings()` before the first RUNNING tick (KRN-BIND-01); there is no window in which `toggle_beam` meets an empty table. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
844	- **If a registrant does not re-register in its own `post_restore`**: nothing is lost (registrations are canonical); a repeat registration is a no-op returning false.
845	- **If a hook id is unknown or creates a cycle at boot** (for example someone registers `after: [emitter.update]`): boot fails loudly (CR-3); only `emitter.place` exists. **If the kernel is FAULTED during a mutator apply**: standard CR-9 handling; every mutator here is Class B or validated, so a fault is a defect.
846	- **If the kernel is `MIRROR`**: it never ticks `emitter.place`; the replica reads `SHARED_SUMMARY`, which in VS-B must carry each beam's origin, aim, shape and switch so a remote crewmate's beam can be drawn.
847	- **If zoom changes**: nothing in the sim changes; an off-screen lit object stays lit and exposes, and the HUD draws no off-screen prompt.
848	
849	**Hallucination and degenerate strategies**

888	**Circularity check.** The index's circular-dependency note says "Lighting exposes an emitter registry; Attention reads it and publishes an attention level; the filament renderer reads both. Lighting never reads Attention." This GDD resolves the first clause: the registry is **`emitter.state`'s read view**, which Lighting and Attention both read, and Lighting never writes it (a wording refresh owed to the index, Cross-References). No cycle exists: Emitter State reads the Graph, the Controller, Body and Layout and none of them reads it back (the Controller's PC-6 *calls* the exposure query, a read, from `validate`, and the Graph reads nothing from here); Attention's `set_beacon` is a `SYSTEM` command applied at T+1.
