The 2D physics ray API is likewise **NOT SOURCEABLE** (`modules/physics.md` carries only a 3D example); EM-20 removes the dependency. 2D physics is unchanged since 4.3 (the reference says so for 4.6). Sourced breaking changes that bite this module (`breaking-changes.md`): 4.7 typed-return overrides need an explicit `return` on every path (a typed-return virtual in an emitter-kind base class would break — avoid virtual dispatch on the hot path); a write to one element of a packed array does not call the property setter, so dirty keys are marked explicitly in the mutators, never in setters (kernel CR-8, Graph LS-18); `duplicate()` is not deep, so snapshot copies use plain-data copies or `duplicate_deep()`. 948	## Visual/Audio Requirements
949	
950	*This block draws and plays nothing. It publishes facts (the emitter read view, the shape table, dirty keys) that the renderer and the audio mixer conform to; every item below is owned by the GDD named in its row and is listed so that the owner's brief is complete. A sentence that needs `Light2D` to be true belongs to 2D Lighting & Occlusion (undesigned; sibling stage), never to this document.*
951	
952	**What is visible.** Light is the only thing this system shows. A beam is a wedge with a **hard outer edge exactly at its reach** (3 screen px of edge, then a soft interior falloff) in the Tungsten hue every human light uses (art bible 4.2); the four shapes, the fan, the deployable pool, the glowstick, the fixture and the beacon are the art bible 8.3 rows (lines 1079–1086) carried verbatim into the shape table, with two rows this GDD adds (lantern, fault glow) and the HARD / SOFT curve classes owed back to 8.3 (Cross-References). A glowstick is Chemlight `#86B896`, steady and then visibly smaller (art bible 3.2: "steady, then waning"); a fixture never flickers (the cryo-bay lamp's gutter is Lighting's, art bible 8.11 flag 2); the dock status glow is a small, dim, steady fixture whose luminance and hue the art-director keeps apart from the visible-unknown lamp (a Lighting `hue_class` token and the luminance separation are owed by the art-director and art bible 7.0 note; X2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; a node lantern is the glow of a running machine in that loop's own hue at its machinery node (art bible 8.3 emission rule, 8.10 flag 8); fault glows are point sources (ember, power arc, cyan O₂ mist) taken from the Failure & Trail descriptor-to-glow table. Everything is drawn from `emitter.state` and nothing else.
953	
954	**What Lighting reads, and must not do.** Lighting reads the per-emitter read view (`id, kind, subkind, shape_id, origin_px, aim_units, half_angle_units, reach_px, r_lit_px, r_off_px, curve_class, output_pm, hue_class, lit, section_id, body_id, priority`, AC-46b) and `shapes()`, and it conforms to them: a texture's reach equals `reach_px` ± 1 px for every hard-edged row; a soft pool's boundary is drawn at max(`r_off_px`, `POOL_RESIDUAL_PX`) ± 1 px (D.7, exact sim values), so that the prompt of an already-lit subject ends exactly where the pool visibly ends and an approaching subject meets its prompt `r_off_px − r_lit_px` px inside it *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* (the sim/render agreement, AC-55 and AC-56, the load-bearing P1 test of the lighting stack); a dimmed emitter is drawn dimmer in proportion to `output_pm` (a lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served, Graph D.6). Lighting **owns** the light textures, ambient and `CanvasModulate`, shadow-slot assignment (lint hypotheses: at most 6 shadow-casting, 24 non-shadow and 8 node lanterns in view, art bible 8.10 and 8.11 flags 2 and 8; "emitters are cut before occlusion"), flicker and gutter, the per-light flash clamp (`flash_count` ≤ 3 per rolling 1 s, pipeline PR-13), and the decoy visuals of the Perception Filter. Lighting **must not**: write an emitter or any block; tell the sim a light is "culled"; give a decoy, a false lamp state or a flicker any query effect (the query reads `output_pm`, not the picture; AC-5a); move the true edge of a real light (art bible Principle 1; the stage-2 "cone seems to reach further" symptom is a **decoy glow past the true edge** with a palette leak, never a wider revealing radius, Cross-References refresh to 4.4); or draw a shadow with no occluder from a horror (actors and horrors never occlude, art bible 3.2, EM-20 c). Occlusion shadows follow the same footprint rectangles the query uses (one source for collision, light and shadow), and the same cell convention: Lighting's occluder polygon for a stored rectangle `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)` is the continuous rectangle covering exactly those pixel cells, and an integer position is the centre of its cell (EM-20 a), so a drawn shadow has no seam where the query has none *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the shadow origin versus the sim's foot segment (EM-6, CP-5) is Open Question 5.
955	
956	**What Audio hears.** Audio keys off the `E/<emitter id>` dirty keys (EM-26) and the Presenter's own pre-play, and reads **no exposure** (it does not call `lux` or `lit`). The beam switch click and the wall-switch click pre-play on input (PC-5; the light itself lands on commit); a lamp hum rises across the 0–5 tick switch latency so the warm-up reads as a ship lamp, not lag; a bank switched together draws inrush and the neighbouring dip is a legitimate, audible, player-caused flicker (Graph `INRUSH_PM`); a glowstick may thin a faint chemical hiss as it wanes and ends with a soft quiet; the beacon's sweep has a rotation cadence at `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` 128 (2.13 s); fault glows share their descriptor's audio (Failure & Trail). **Light itself is silent**: this system emits no noise into Attention's intake (noise is a tool property, PC-10).

972	
973	## Game Feel
974	
975	*A real note, not a template fill: this system has no animation, no input of its own and no hit; its feel is the **honesty and timing of light**. The feel of the toggle's input belongs to the Player Controller (PC-5 and its debounce; the sim-side `TOO_SOON` floor beneath it is EM-7), the feel of how light looks to 2D Lighting & Occlusion, the feel of every sound to Audio; this GDD owns the numbers underneath them, which are below.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
976	
977	**Feel reference.** The chest lamp should feel like Pandorum's helmet light and the Alien: Isolation torch in one respect only: it is *yours*, hands-free, always where you are facing, and it is the one thing in the game that never lies. The ship's lamps should feel like a machine that has to be served: they come up with the ship, not ahead of it.
978	
979	**Input responsiveness (beam).** The `toggle_beam` press applies at P2 and the light is committed in the same tick's `emitter.place`: zero internal latency, at most one tick (16.7 ms) from apply to the lit state the renderer sees, inside the Controller's ≤ 17 ms click-to-commit budget (PC-5). The click and the switch animation pre-play; the **light never does** (the Presenter never predicts beam state: the lamp is the human-channel anchor and may not lie for one frame). Turn-off is immediate. Feel target: decisive, mechanical, slightly heavy; never a lag the player reads as the game being slow, never a flash the player reads as the game being wrong.
980	
981	**Ship lamps warm; the chest lamp snaps.** A fixture switched on is ARMING until the Graph serves it: 0 to `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` − 1 ticks (0–83 ms), below perception on its own, and Audio's relay clunk and hum rise fill it so it reads as a ship lamp, not as lag. Under a weak bus a bank of lamps switched together draws `INRUSH_PM` 1500 for `INRUSH_STEPS` 5 Graph runs (0.5 s): the neighbouring lamps dip (the Graph example is 945 permille) and recover. That dip is an honest, audible, **player-caused** flicker and the best single lesson the ship teaches about load; it must never be smoothed away.
982	
983	**The rim.** At full output the edge of a HARD emitter is a step (about 252 permille inside, 0 outside; `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` 250 with `LIT_ON_PM` 150), so an object pops into reach at an exact pixel. The 150 / 120 hysteresis never sees that step; it bites only on **dimmed** emitters (brownout, waning glowsticks) whose interior crosses the threshold band, so a prompt does not strobe in a fade. While the aim is sweeping, committed-versus-drawn divergence of up to 2.8° and ≤ 3 ticks (PC-5) moves the rim by about 14 px at 288 px (WIDE) and 19 px at 384 px (NARROW); a rim object may prompt a few ticks late and rim chatter is held by the Controller's `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN`, not by this block. The edge-agreement test (design test 1) holds **at rest and for full-output emitters**; a dimmed light's actionable area shrinks honestly (a fixture at 500 permille loses prompts for objects within 22 px of its full-output readable edge (`r_lit` falls from 122 to 100 px): "the junction box at the edge went out of reach when the scrubber drew").
984	
985	**Glowstick wane and beacon.** A glowstick is steady for its first 60 % of life, then shrinks over the rest in visible integer steps; the shrinking pool is the only clock and no number is ever shown. A stick put out by the live cap is never snuffed: it takes the same visible shrink, faster (10 s, D.9b), so the pool still only ever dies by shrinking. The beacon lights a point for 14 or 15 of every 128 ticks, so it is *seen* and never gates a prompt (EM-16): nothing strobes at the sweep rate.
986	
987	**The split beam's dark wedge is its identity.** Two cones at ±18° off the aim with a wedge of at least 16° that never closes: the one shape that cannot see straight ahead. It is a loadout personality, not a bug; nobody should "fix" it.
988	
989	**Impact moments.** (1) A brownout takes the corridor lamps down and, when power returns, the corridor beyond is exactly where it was (the world never lied). (2) A glowstick thrown into the next room: the pool blooms Chemlight green on landing, not in flight. (3) A lamp bank clicking on and the whole deck sagging for half a second. (4) The tell: filaments resolving at the cone edge, which needs this stable edge to resolve at.
990	
991	**Feel acceptance.** AC-FEEL (manual, retained screenshots, technical-artist and game-designer sign-off) covers the toggle, the inrush dip, the rim at rest at three zoom rungs, and the glowstick wane. Weight and responsiveness profile: instant for the beam and turn-off, 0–5 ticks for a fixture, 0.5 s for a bank dip, 150 s for a glowstick.
992	
993	## UI Requirements
994	
995	**No UI of its own.** This system draws no HUD element, menu, instrument or world-space marker, and none is permitted: no exposure bar, ring, icon, "light level" or visibility readout, and no marker on a lit or unlit object (P3: shown in the world, never a meter; Attention is likewise a thing the world does). The only gameplay surface that follows from this block is a **prompt that is present or absent**, and its drawing is owned elsewhere. The surfaces below are the readers of this block's answers; each states what it needs and from where.

The prompt must not flicker faster than the Controller's focus stickiness allows (hysteresis is this block's, rim stickiness the Controller's). The inspect card appears only on a lit instrument. 205:d stages it (SL-11), from the hot in-memory copy of the newest verified generation where one exists (SL-11). It then computes the advanced `restore_epoch` (SL-23 (1)), hands its `slot_epoch.bin` write to the worker and polls it once per frame (SL-23 (2), never blocking the main thread). Only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`, or after the write's logged failure or timeout (`SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE`, `save_status = FAILED`), does it call `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)`, which the kernel honours at that boundary's services, normally the first boundary after `DEAD` (the Controller's `DEAD` row and its Edge Case "`DEAD` entered during a camera cut" conform, R14) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — deleg

I'm noting that Layout's documented call order is informational, not a hard rule, so OQ 26 remains unresolved — the ordering dependency belongs to the Emitter, not Layout. If Emitter's post_restore executes before Layout's version bump, it would read a stale version and a closed-leaf geometry before Layout updates things.

This creates a mismatch at the first RUNNING tick's P2 validate step, comparing cold-table closed leaves against the uninterrupted run's open leaf — a G4 hazard that EM-28 claims has no accepted exception, and which I flagged as RECOMMENDED in a prior review but remains unresolved. The AC-30/AC-54 snapshot tests with real Layout would also likely fail on door-open ticks, and I don't see a simple fix beyond having Emitter re-check version during the first tick.

With the body_id blocker now resolved, I'm going through the remaining RECOMMENDED items — starting with the state machine gaps around E10-off and ABSENT→STARVED transitions, which I confirm are still not resolved by checking the ABSENT row's listed transitions, which lack a STARVED path, and the ON row's who-may-cause list, which omits E10.

Tracing through the OFF→STARVED row for PLAYER ON on a FAILED node, I conclude it's just a redundant/ambiguous restatement of the OFF→ARMING→STARVED path that already works through existing rows, so that part is fine. But I notice another gap: an idle NODE_LANTERN at init_world with zero run_pm should produce STARVED output, yet the only listed ABSENT transition is to ON for a live lantern — there's no corresponding ABSENT→STARVED transition documented for this idle case, while FAULT_GLOW only ever transitions to ON since it's created only when output is positive.

This gap means `emitter_invalid_transition` could fire during normal gameplay if the lantern starts idle, which would break AC-116's expectation that this validator doesn't fire in the happy path — so I'm keeping its severity as RECOMMENDED rather than downgrading it. Separately, EM-28's restore equivalence against OQ26 remains unresolved, and for the COOLDOWN feedback issue, I need to check whether the Interaction system actually references the COOLDOWN term to confirm the cue fires as expected by AC-90c.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria: AC-109 (line 1240)
findings.finding: Untestable as written (carried over). Quote: 'GIVEN an emitter in WANING and a command that would move it to OFF, or any transition not listed ... THEN the state is unchanged, emitter_invalid_transition increments by 1'. No public command can produce this: set_switch on a deployable is rejected NOT_SWITCHABLE at validate and never reaches state logic, so the stimulus does not exist through the API and the criterion cannot fail.
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'GIVEN the lifecycle table as a fixture and the internal transition seam apply_transition(record, to), WHEN each (from,to) pair absent from the tables is driven through the seam, THEN the record is unchanged and emitter_invalid_transition increments by 1 labelled (from,to); AND GIVEN every listed pair, THEN it increments 0; AND GIVEN the AC-1 600-tick script plus a weld, a cut, a pod hop and a dock departure, THEN the counter reads 0.' Add the seam to the harness list.

findings.section: EM-28 (line 278), Open Question 26 (line 1360), AC-30 / AC-54
findings.finding: EM-28 still claims save-equivalence holds 'with no accepted exception', yet the same paragraph and OQ 26 admit it depends on Layout's post_restore running before the Emitter's cold static build. Kernel CR-8 (line 114) still only says post_restore runs 'after all blocks restore' and Layout line 302 calls the post_restore order 'informational only'. If Layout's runs second, the first P2 validate after a restore with an open door reads the leaves-closed table, which differs from the uninterrupted run; AC-30 and AC-54 (restore at every tick, real Layout) would fail on door-open ticks. MVP death is restart-from-autosave, so restore is on the main path.
findings.fix: Either (a) get the kernel to grant 'post_restore calls follow restore_after' (CR-8) and close OQ 26, or (b) make the Emitter robust without it: in post_restore re-read Layout leaf rectangles lazily (treat the cold build as leaf-region dirty and re-test leaf-adjacent pairs inside the same restore, before the first RUNNING tick). Reword EM-28 to say which, and give AC-54 a door-open fixture.

findings.section: EM-9 (line 210), States table DEAD row (line 324), Edge Cases (line 801), AC-13c (line 1160), Cross-References (line 1025)
findings.finding: Stale against delegated ruling R14. The GDD says the DEAD-tick forced beam-off is 'unobservable in the MVP because the death stub restarts from the last autosave through request_restore at that tick's P6'. Under R14 Save/Load stages a durable slot_epoch.bin write first and calls request_restore only after EPOCH_DURABLE, normally one frame later and up to RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS (30 frames); the kernel stays RUNNING with the seat DEAD in the meantime (save-load-and-versioned-format.md lines 205, 286). The forced-off beam is therefore observable for 1 to 30 ticks. Harmless, but 'say so in tests' now asserts something untrue.
findings.fix: Reword the four sites to: 'the beam is forced off at the DEAD tick and stays off during the Save/Load epoch-staging interval (1 to 30 ticks) until the restore replaces it'. AC-13c keeps testing the isolated emitter and adds 'toggle_beam rejected NOT_ACTIONABLE for the staging ticks'.

findings.section: EM-7 / EM-25 beam_bindings (lines 169, 262), EM-1, EM-5; whole GDD (zero mentions of ctx)
findings.finding: Not yet conformed to delegated ruling R3 (kernel CR-19b, command-simulation-layer.md lines 96, 112, 114). The kernel now requires every owner callable to receive ctx, report via ctx.ok()/ctx.reject(reason), deliver data through ctx.put, and return only ctx.complete() (never -> void). This GDD describes beam_bindings() as a read-view entry returning [(player_id, beam_id)] and describes toggle_beam/set_switch/set_beacon validate/apply, snapshot and post_restore with no ctx anywhere. An implementer following this GDD would write a binding source the kernel's LOADING rebuild rejects.
findings.fix: Per G1 the kernel owns the convention: restate beam_bindings as a CR-7 binding source with ctx (pure read, ctx.put of the ascending pairs, return ctx.complete()), add one sentence in EM-1/EM-5 that every owner callable (validate, apply, snapshot, restore, post_restore, read_view) follows CR-19, and adjust AC-15b to read the delivered pairs.

findings.finding: Untestable as written (carried over). Quote: 'GIVEN an emitter in WANING and a command that would move it to OFF, or any transition not listed ...
